title: Flexible neural population dynamics govern the speed and stability of sensory encoding in mouse visual cortex
goal: Reproduce the complete original five-mouse Figure 2h and Figure 4d,e findings on how stationary versus locomotion states alter the time course and temporal stability of six-speed information in V1. Preserve original state/trial/neuron eligibility, within-time curves, cross-time matrices, relative-generalization numerator and denominator, paired mouse-level state/time effects and indispensable original statistics. Assess improvement of this same empirical finding only under an independently justified scientific criterion; higher decoder accuracy or a larger state effect alone does not establish it.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable analysis and source-native outputs for the corrected primary empirical findings: The complete original five-mouse Figure 2h/4d,e empirical state/time decoding finding, preserving within-time curves, state/train/test-time matrices, relative cross-time generalization and its numerator/denominator, paired mouse-level effects and source-required controls. The Allen extension and other figures remain outside this task.
Primary improvement: unavailable until a source-grounded same-result comparison is independently justified; no new score or direction is implied.

Retained secondary work: Preserve source-native state-specific six-class decoding accuracy and cross-time generalization as a legitimate, separately named empirical method-performance comparison on the original inputs, support and protocols. It is not preprocessing or simulation; a qualified method-performance gain must not automatically become improved biological explanation or current SOTA. Preserve the chronological pooled-state calibration/decoding protocol as a distinct prospective adaptation. Preserve scientific opportunities to challenge the original state/time finding; do not require a candidate to increase the locomotion effect or force agreement with its direction.
success_criteria: Recreate the corrected primary empirical findings with their source-defined populations, complete required panels and controls.
Use an explicitly bound reproduction proposal only within its declared eligibility, comparison and execution limits; copying published findings is insufficient.

The preserved improvement.v1.json retains its declared comparison and coverage. Use retained_secondary_scope for its relationship to the corrected primary findings; satisfying a secondary or partial-component criterion alone does not establish complete primary reproduction or improvement.

The primary same-target outcome bundle is unavailable. Any primary improvement requires an independently justified source-grounded comparison; no replacement metric, direction or tolerance is invented.
Keep the paper+data and paper+data+author-code outcomes separate. All scientific outcomes remain unknown until qualifying original-data execution and independent verification.
Preserve prior task definitions, improvement criteria and useful secondary implementations with their original scopes. Historical attempts and source metadata do not become qualified AI results.
